title: Illinois insurance pre-licensing school (live-webinar hours + self-paced) sold B2C and to recruiting agencies
product_service: IDOI-certified 20-hour-per-line pre-licensing courses (Life, Accident/Health, Property, Casualty) including the mandatory 7.5 live classroom/webinar hours per line, plus exam-prep question bank; B2B packages for captive/independent agencies, Medicare FMOs and carriers that recruit and sponsor new agents.
target_customer: Individuals entering insurance sales in Illinois; recruiting managers at captive agencies (State Farm/Allstate-type agency owners), IMOs/FMOs, call-center insurance distributors that pay for recruits' licensing.
purchase_motivation: Statutory mandate: no exam eligibility without certified pre-licensing hours; employers need licensed producers fast to bill.
spending_evidence: Illinois Part-1 exam attempts Jan 2022–Jan 2023: Life 6,071, Accident/Health 3,986, Property 3,005, Casualty 3,143 (~16.2k attempts incl. retakes) [A, WS09-S001]; 20 hours per line with 7.5 classroom/webinar hours mandated [A, WS09-S002; C, WS09-S016]. Course price levels in Illinois not captured (MISSING).
representative_operators: Aceable Insurance — national venture-backed online provider marketing Illinois L&H [C, WS09-S016]
Kaplan Financial Education, ExamFX, AD Banker, WebCE — national incumbents (named from industry knowledge; sizes MISSING) [E]
revenue_mechanism: Price per line/bundle x students; B2B volume contracts with agencies (prepaid seat packs).
typical_transaction_value: Est. $100–$350 per student for one or two lines [E; Illinois price points not verified]
direct_costs: Live webinar instructor time (7.5 hrs/line/cohort), LMS/platform fees, payment processing, provider/course approval fees (amounts MISSING), content updates.
contribution_profit_note: If a live cohort of 20 students x $200 = $4,000 against ~$600 instructor + $300 platform/processing, contribution ~ $3,000/cohort [E].
working_capital_note: Paid upfront by card or prepaid B2B seat packs; negligible receivables; no inventory.
sales_cycle: B2C impulse/short (days); B2B agency deals 2–8 weeks.
repeat_purchase: occasional — one-time per student; B2B agencies recruit continuously (recurring cohorts); CE (24 hrs/2 yrs, unverified) is an adjacent recurring product.
acquisition_channels: Google search ads on 'Illinois insurance license class'
Referral from insurance carriers' recruiting teams
customer_accessibility: Agency owners are identifiable from IDOI producer lookups and carrier agent locators; B2C searchers are reachable but auction-priced by national players.
supplier_accessibility: Assumed: content can be authored by founder after obtaining a producer license; course certification via IDOI/state-based systems (process and fees not verified).
competitive_intensity: high — national online incumbents with SEO, brand and multi-state catalogs; some carriers run in-house schools.
entry_strategy: Own the live-hours requirement for Illinois with evening/weekend live webinars in English and Spanish, pass guarantee, and B2B seat packs with recruit tracking for agency owners; ancillary CE for the same agencies.
licenses: IDOI education provider/course certification required (fees/timeline MISSING) [A, WS09-S002]; instructor qualification rules MISSING; founder can obtain a producer license in ~1–2 months (exam $92, license $215) [C, WS09-S016].
regulatory_barriers: Course approval and audit; live-hour attendance verification; content must track exam outline changes.
operational_risks: Pass rates drive reputation; instructor quality; scheduling enough cohorts.
financial_risks: Small Illinois-only pool; price pressure from national players; dependence on a few agency accounts.
geographic_constraints: Illinois-specific approval; multi-state requires separate approvals per state.
founder_expertise: Insurance fundamentals (get licensed), instructional design, live teaching, B2B selling to agency owners.
staffing: Founder teaches first; add 1–3 part-time licensed instructors by year 2; part-time student support.
automation_potential: AI-generated question banks and explanations, automated enrollment/attendance logs, recruit-progress dashboards for agencies. Live hours stay human.
delegation_potential: Moderate–good: instructors and support are standard roles; approvals/compliance remain owner tasks.
scalability: Illinois pool limited (~10–12k unique candidates/yr est. from ~16k attempts [E]); growth requires multi-state approvals and CE.
expansion: Insurance CE, Medicare AHIP-adjacent prep, P&C agency staff training, adjacent Midwest states.
roic_note: Low capital (<$25k) so ROIC high if it works, but absolute profit small.
critical_assumptions: A newcomer can win 5–10% via live-hour scheduling and agency deals
IDOI provider approval obtainable in <6 months at modest cost
unanswered_questions: IDOI education provider approval process, fees, instructor qualifications
Illinois price points for pre-licensing packages
Share of candidates sponsored by employers
Post-2025 exam volumes after online proctoring ended
failure_modes: Cannot outrank/outspend national players on search
Thin Illinois volume after splitting with carrier in-house schools
Pass rates below competitors damage referrals
score_rationale: fcf 3: Illinois pool too small for >$120k profit without multi-state. resilience 6: mandated seat-time is AI-resistant even if AI tutors erode prep value. entry 3: crowded by national online brands; live-hour/B2B wedge is copyable. cash 8: prepaid.
preliminary_verdict: hold — mandated, real counted demand, but small Illinois pool and strong national incumbents cap profit.

title: Illinois real estate pre-license / post-license / CE school with in-person Applied Principles wedge
product_service: IDFPR-licensed education provider offering the 75-hour broker pre-license (60-hr Topics any format + 15-hr Applied Real Estate Principles in classroom/equivalent), 45-hour post-license, 12-hour CE (6 core + 6 elective incl. sexual harassment prevention), and exam prep; sold to individuals and brokerages.
target_customer: Aspiring brokers in Chicagoland; brokerages recruiting agents; licensed brokers renewing every two years.
purchase_motivation: Statutory mandate for licensure and renewal [A, WS09-S017].
spending_evidence: Online 75-hr packages priced $399/$519/$699 by AceableAgent [B, WS09-S015]; renewal requires CE/post-license by April 30, 2026 [A, WS09-S007, WS09-S017]. Illinois broker headcount and annual new licensees MISSING.
representative_operators: ~50 IDFPR-approved pre-license providers incl. Colibri Real Estate, Kaplan, AceableAgent, Real Estate U, community colleges, REALTOR associations and many small Chicago schools [A, WS09-S028]
revenue_mechanism: Tuition per course/package; CE packages; brokerage group contracts.
typical_transaction_value: $399–$699 pre-license package (competitor list) [B, WS09-S015]; CE packages est. $50–$150 [E].
direct_costs: Licensed instructors for classroom/live hours, classroom rent, proctored exams (every 15 hours per rule summary), LMS, $1,050 provider + $150/course fees [A, WS09-S006].
contribution_profit_note: A 15-hr in-person Applied Principles cohort of 20 at est. $150–$200 add-on = $3–4k vs ~$1k instructor/room [E].
working_capital_note: Prepaid tuition; no receivables except brokerage invoices.
repeat_purchase: recurring-contract — licensees need CE every 2 years; post-license once.
acquisition_channels: Partnering with national online schools that need in-person 15-hr delivery (hypothesis)
customer_accessibility: Brokerages and brokers are public via IDFPR lookup; consumers reachable but ad costs set by national players.
supplier_accessibility: Need IDFPR-licensed pre-license instructors (licensing steps MISSING); founder not licensed.
competitive_intensity: extreme — ~50 approved providers incl. PE/VC-backed national brands [A, WS09-S028].
entry_strategy: Be the best-scheduled in-person 15-hour Applied Principles and exam-cram provider in specific suburbs/languages, and license CE to brokerages as a private-label school.
licenses: IDFPR Education Provider license ($1,050) + $150 per course; licensed instructors; registered entity [A, WS09-S006].
regulatory_barriers: Course approvals, proctoring rules, instructor licensing; single published fee schedule for all students [A, WS09-S006].
operational_risks: Instructor supply; classroom utilization; curriculum changes.
financial_risks: Housing-cycle sensitivity of new-agent inflows; national price competition.
founder_expertise: Real estate law/practice content; would need licensed instructors or own broker license (pre-license course + exam).
automation_potential: AI-written practice questions, adaptive drills, automated CE tracking; classroom hours remain human.
delegation_potential: Moderate: classroom teaching delegable to licensed instructors.
scalability: Low–moderate; Illinois-capped, multi-state would compete with national brands.
expansion: Appraiser/leasing agent/managing broker courses; mortgage and insurance prelicense cross-sell.
roic_note: Low capital; returns limited by volume not capital.
critical_assumptions: In-person 15-hr requirement creates local demand online players cannot fully absorb
unanswered_questions: Number of active Illinois brokers and annual new licensees
Whether national online schools already partner for in-person hours
failure_modes: Brokerage in-house schools (e.g., brokerage-owned providers on list)
score_rationale: entry 2: ~50 licensed competitors incl. national brands. resilience 4: mandated but tied to housing cycle. fcf 2: realistic profit well under $100k.
preliminary_verdict: reject — mandated but saturated; at best a side line to another education business.

title: Online CDL Entry-Level Driver Training (ELDT) theory + CDL permit prep (national)
product_service: FMCSA-registered online ELDT theory curriculum (Class A/B, upgrades, hazmat, passenger/school bus) with TPR certification upload, plus CDL permit-test prep; sold B2C and white-labeled to carriers/behind-the-wheel schools.
target_customer: CDL applicants nationally; motor carriers training new drivers; small BTW schools lacking theory content.
purchase_motivation: Federal mandate since Feb 2022: ELDT completion must be in TPR before skills test.
spending_evidence: TPR shows 34,876 drivers trained in Oct 2026 and 2,093,602 since Feb 2022 (~440k/yr) [A, WS09-S023]. Theory price levels MISSING.
representative_operators: 18,384 active registered providers [A, WS09-S023]; >10,000 removed in enforcement since Dec 2025 [C, WS09-S020]
revenue_mechanism: Per-student fee; per-seat B2B licensing to carriers/schools.
direct_costs: LMS hosting, content maintenance, TPR submissions, support, payment fees, ads.
contribution_profit_note: Digital marginal cost near zero; contribution driven by CAC [E].
customer_accessibility: Carriers identifiable via FMCSA data; consumers via search (crowded).
supplier_accessibility: Content self-authored against federal curriculum; no supplier dependency.
competitive_intensity: extreme — 18k+ registered providers, many free-with-employment carrier programs.
entry_strategy: Weak; only plausible wedge is multilingual theory + compliance-proof records for small BTW schools facing FMCSA crackdown.
licenses: FMCSA TPR self-registration; state requirements for schools vary (Illinois SOS rules not verified) [A, WS09-S023].
regulatory_barriers: FMCSA enforcement removing non-compliant providers (raises compliance burden but also clears field) [C, WS09-S020].
financial_risks: Commoditized pricing; freight-cycle sensitivity of driver demand.
founder_expertise: FMCSA curriculum, CDL knowledge (founder may need CDL experience for credibility).
automation_potential: High: AI tutors, translation, automated TPR submissions — but equally available to competitors.
expansion: Behind-the-wheel school (WS09-004), hazmat/tanker endorsements, carrier compliance training.
roic_note: Low capital, but CAC likely eats margin.
critical_assumptions: Theory can be differentiated by language/compliance features
unanswered_questions: Market price distribution for ELDT theory
Share of drivers trained free by carriers
Illinois SOS requirements for driver-training schools
score_rationale: entry 2: 18k providers. resilience 5: federal mandate but tied to freight cycle. fcf 2: commodity.
preliminary_verdict: reject — real federal mandate but saturated commodity market.

title: Chicago-area CDL behind-the-wheel training school with carrier/WIOA-funded students
product_service: Behind-the-wheel (range + road) Class A/B training with ELDT theory, skills-test readiness, and job placement with carriers; tuition paid by students, employers (tuition reimbursement) or workforce grants.
target_customer: Career changers; local/regional carriers, municipalities, school bus contractors needing drivers.
purchase_motivation: Federal ELDT mandate plus persistent driver demand; employers pay to fill seats.
spending_evidence: ~440k ELDT completions/yr nationally [A, WS09-S023]; Illinois tuition levels, WIOA ITA caps MISSING.
representative_operators: Thousands of TPR-registered BTW locations (31,172 active locations nationally) [A, WS09-S023]; community colleges and carrier schools (names/sizes MISSING)
revenue_mechanism: Tuition per student (cohort-based) + placement fees from carriers (where legal).
direct_costs: Instructors (CDL holders), trucks/trailers (lease or used), fuel, insurance, range/yard rent, maintenance, test fees.
contribution_profit_note: Est. $1,500–$3,000 per student after instructor, fuel, truck cost [E].
working_capital_note: Tuition prepaid or financed; WIOA/agency payments can lag 30–90 days [E].
repeat_purchase: none per student; recurring employer pipelines.
customer_accessibility: Moderate: workforce boards and carriers identifiable; students reachable through ads.
supplier_accessibility: Used tractors/trailers available; commercial insurance for training fleets may be costly (unverified).
competitive_intensity: high — many schools, community colleges, carrier-paid training.
entry_strategy: High pass rate + placement network + Spanish/Polish instruction + school-bus/municipal Class B niche.
licenses: FMCSA TPR registration; Illinois Secretary of State commercial driver training school licensing and IBHE vocational rules likely (not verified) [E].
regulatory_barriers: School licensing, instructor qualifications, insurance; FMCSA audits [C, WS09-S020].
financial_risks: Capital tied in trucks; freight recession cuts demand; funding-agency delays.
founder_expertise: Trucking operations; regulatory compliance; instructor hiring.
automation_potential: Scheduling, admissions, AI theory tutoring; driving instruction stays human.
expansion: Hazmat, school-bus, forklift, heavy equipment operator training.
roic_note: Capital $40–120k at risk; ROIC moderate; fleet leasing improves.
unanswered_questions: Illinois SOS/IBHE licensing steps and timeline
failure_modes: Unable to get on funding lists
score_rationale: fcf 4: real tuition tickets but capital/insurance heavy. feasibility 5: school licensing + insurance unknowns. resilience 5: cyclical freight demand.
preliminary_verdict: hold — more substantial ticket than online prep, but capital/insurance/licensing unknowns need screening.

title: Paid Illinois sexual-harassment-prevention training (B2B annual compliance)
product_service: Annual Illinois-compliant harassment prevention e-learning or live sessions with completion tracking and restaurant/bar supplemental module, sold to small/mid employers.
target_customer: Illinois employers (all sizes; every employer with an Illinois employee).
purchase_motivation: Annual statutory mandate (775 ILCS 5/2-109) [A, WS09-S024].
spending_evidence: Mandate is universal, but IDHR provides free model training, free public sessions, and free private group sessions [A, WS09-S003, WS09-S024]; paid market size MISSING.
representative_operators: IDHR (free) [A, WS09-S024]
HR/payroll platforms and LMS vendors bundling compliance courses (names/sizes not verified) [E]
revenue_mechanism: Per-employee per-year fee or bundle.
direct_costs: LMS, content updates, support; trainer time for live sessions.
contribution_profit_note: High margin per seat but tiny tickets; CAC per small employer likely exceeds annual fee [E].
customer_accessibility: Employers reachable, but free state option undercuts.
supplier_accessibility: Content self-authored.
competitive_intensity: extreme — free government product plus bundled HR-platform offerings.
entry_strategy: None durable; only as a bundle inside a broader compliance service (see WS09-007/008).
licenses: None [A, WS09-S024].
automation_potential: AI can produce/translate content cheaply — which also commoditizes it.
expansion: Multi-state harassment training (CA, NY, CT, DE, ME also mandate) — crowded.
critical_assumptions: Employers pay for convenience over free IDHR model
unanswered_questions: Share of employers using paid vendors vs free model
score_rationale: entry 1: state gives it away free. fcf 1: no path to meaningful profit standalone. evidence A for the killer fact (free model).
preliminary_verdict: reject — a universal mandate the state itself satisfies for free; at most a bundle feature.

target_customer: Illinois on-premise alcohol servers and ID checkers; bar/restaurant owners.

supplier_accessibility: Content self-authored; ILCC licensing steps not verified.
competitive_intensity: extreme — $14.99 national online offerings.

Number of BASSET certificates issued per year

title: Chicagoland restaurant compliance-training bundle (CFPM classes/proctoring in multiple languages + food handler, allergen, BASSET, harassment supplemental, renewal tracking)
product_service: Done-for-you compliance program for independent restaurants: in-person/live CFPM courses with proctored ANSI exams (as authorized instructor/proctor of an accredited program), resale of ANSI food handler and allergen courses, BASSET via licensed partner or own license, harassment supplemental module, and a renewal-tracking portal that warns before inspections.
target_customer: Owners/GMs of independent and small-chain restaurants, bars, caterers, grocery delis in Chicago metro, especially non-English-dominant operators.
purchase_motivation: Health-department inspection compliance (CFPM on site, food handler within 30 days, 3-yr renewals) [A, WS09-S009; C, WS09-S027]; BASSET 3-yr mandate [B, WS09-S004]; avoiding citations/closures.
spending_evidence: Mandates documented [A, WS09-S009]; BASSET online at $14.99 [B, WS09-S014]; CFPM class/exam prices in Chicago MISSING (est. $125–$200) [E].
representative_operators: ServSafe/National Restaurant Association and its independent instructor network (sizes MISSING) [E]
StateFoodSafety, 360training (online) [C, WS09-S027; B, WS09-S014]
revenue_mechanism: Per-person class/exam fees + annual per-location compliance subscription (tracking + scheduling) + reseller margin on online courses.
typical_transaction_value: Est. $150–$200 per CFPM candidate; est. $300–$900/location/yr subscription [E].
direct_costs: Exam vouchers/course wholesale from accredited program, instructor/proctor time, classroom rental, software.
contribution_profit_note: Class of 12 CFPM x $175 = $2,100 vs est. ~$900 exam/books/room/instructor -> ~$1,200 per class [E].
working_capital_note: Prepaid by restaurants; vouchers bought ahead in small lots.
sales_cycle: Days–weeks; often triggered by inspection or new hire.
repeat_purchase: recurring-contract — CFPM every 5 yrs (unverified), food handler/BASSET every 3 yrs, harassment annual, high staff turnover.
acquisition_channels: Door-to-door/phone to restaurants (public food license lists)
Restaurant supply distributors and POS resellers as referral partners
customer_accessibility: Good: thousands of licensed food establishments are public via city/county license data; owners reachable in person.
supplier_accessibility: Assumed: accredited CFPM exam providers (e.g., ServSafe, NRFSP, Prometric) allow independent instructors/proctors; terms not verified.
competitive_intensity: high — national online + many independent instructors; multilingual in-person + tracking is a thinner field (unverified).
entry_strategy: Language-specific in-person classes plus a compliance-calendar service that removes the owner's tracking burden; sell to restaurant groups and through distributors.
licenses: Accredited program instructor/proctor approval (MISSING); ILCC license if teaching BASSET [B, WS09-S004]; no professional license.
regulatory_barriers: Low; must use ANSI/ANAB-accredited programs [A, WS09-S009].
operational_risks: Instructor quality; exam security; scheduling density.
financial_risks: Low capital; low ticket requires volume.
geographic_constraints: Local delivery for classes; tracking scalable.
founder_expertise: Food code basics (get CFPM), proctor certification, sales to small business owners.
automation_potential: Renewal tracking, reminders, multilingual AI translation of study aids, scheduling. Classes/proctoring human.
delegation_potential: Good: instructors and schedulers standard roles.
scalability: Metro-limited unless replicated; ceiling likely ~$1–2M revenue.
expansion: OSHA/forklift for food manufacturers (WS09-008), pest/sanitation vendor referrals, multi-city.
roic_note: Very low capital; ROIC high, absolute dollars modest.
critical_assumptions: Restaurants pay a subscription for tracking
unanswered_questions: CFPM course/exam wholesale cost and instructor terms
Chicago CFPM class prices and volumes
Allergen training requirement details for Illinois
failure_modes: Free health-dept classes or online substitutes
score_rationale: resilience 7: stacked recurring mandates, AI cannot sit an exam. access 6: public license lists, walk-in sales. fcf 3/scale 3: small tickets, local.
preliminary_verdict: hold — mandated, accessible, cheap to test; profit ceiling likely below $150k.

title: On-site B2B workplace-safety training contractor (forklift/PIT, OSHA 10/30 classroom via authorized trainers, HAZCOM, bilingual) for Chicago-area warehouses and plants
product_service: Trainers go to client sites to deliver forklift/powered-industrial-truck operator training and evaluations, OSHA 10/30 Outreach (classroom by OSHA-authorized trainers), HAZCOM/lockout-tagout/heat awareness, in English/Spanish/Polish, plus records and 3-year re-evaluation scheduling.
target_customer: EHS/HR/plant managers at warehouses, 3PLs, manufacturers, distributors, staffing agencies (50–1,000 employees) in Chicago metro.
purchase_motivation: OSHA training obligations (e.g., PIT operator training/evaluation and re-evaluation at least every 3 years — regulation not fetched in this pass [E]); citations, insurance-carrier loss-control demands, onboarding throughput.
spending_evidence: OSHA online outreach limited to 8 authorized providers, so in-person/authorized-trainer delivery is the open channel [A, WS09-S018]; trainers need 5 yrs safety experience [A, WS09-S005]; per-session prices MISSING.
representative_operators: Safety consultancies, equipment dealers' training departments, community college customized training (names/sizes MISSING) [E]
Online-only national providers listed by OSHA [A, WS09-S018]
revenue_mechanism: Per-session/day rate or per-trainee fee; annual training retainers with multi-site clients; card processing fees.
typical_transaction_value: Est. $900–$2,500 per on-site session/day; est. $75–$175 per forklift trainee [E].
direct_costs: Trainer wages (authorized trainers/experienced safety pros), travel, OSHA card fees, materials, liability insurance.
contribution_profit_note: Day of training at $1,800 vs trainer $500–$700 + travel/materials $100 -> ~$1,000 contribution [E].
working_capital_note: Net-30 B2B invoices; low inventory; payroll ahead of collections.
repeat_purchase: recurring-contract — new-hire flows, 3-year forklift re-evaluations, annual refreshers.
acquisition_channels: Staffing agencies and forklift dealers as partners
customer_accessibility: Good: industrial employers identifiable via public data/LinkedIn; frequent need; referrals common.
supplier_accessibility: Need experienced trainers; OSHA-authorized trainers are an existing labor pool (availability/cost MISSING).
competitive_intensity: moderate — fragmented local consultancies and dealers; few bilingual-at-scale providers (unverified).
entry_strategy: Fast scheduling (within a week), bilingual delivery, shift-friendly sessions, digital certification records with re-evaluation reminders; target staffing agencies who need throughput.
licenses: No state license; OSHA outreach requires authorized trainer (#500/#501 prerequisites) [A, WS09-S005]; general liability insurance.
regulatory_barriers: Trainer credential requirements limit founder delivering OSHA cards personally.
operational_risks: Trainer availability; injury during practical evaluations; quality consistency.
founder_expertise: Safety regulations, sales to industrial buyers; founder can become a forklift trainer (no formal credential required, unverified) but not an OSHA outreach trainer without 5 yrs experience.
automation_potential: Scheduling, record-keeping, reminder automation, AI translation of handouts; delivery and evaluation remain human.
delegation_potential: Good: trainers + ops coordinator; standard roles.
scalability: Regional; multiple metros possible; ceiling ~$2–3M revenue est.
expansion: HAZWOPER, DOT hazmat, first aid/CPR (instructor certs), safety consulting, Spanish-language supervisor training.
roic_note: Asset-light; returns limited by trainer margin and sales capacity.
unanswered_questions: Local market prices for forklift/OSHA classes
Exact text of 29 CFR 1910.178(l) re-evaluation rules
score_rationale: access 6: many frequent-need buyers. resilience 6: mandated, in-person, AI-proof delivery, but cyclical. fcf 4: service margins ~40–60%.
preliminary_verdict: advance — one of the few WS09 models where the mandate plus in-person delivery resists AI and is reachable by direct B2B sales; needs price/trainer-cost validation.

title: Free, sponsor-funded niche B2B trade newsletter for an underserved Midwest industry vertical (Industry Dive model, small scale)
product_service: Daily/weekly email newsletter + website with original reporting for one industrial/service vertical (e.g., Midwest distributors, municipal public works, specialty trades), monetized by sponsorships, native ads, webinars and job listings.
target_customer: Readers: operators/managers in the vertical (free). Payers: vendors selling into that vertical (marketing managers).
purchase_motivation: Vendors pay for targeted reach to hard-to-find B2B buyers.
spending_evidence: Industry Dive (free B2B trade newsletters) reached ~$110m revenue / $34m EBITDA in 2022 and sold for $389m cash (~11x EBITDA) [B, WS09-S010] — incumbent economics after years and dozens of verticals.
